Swamy M.N vs Sathya Prakash on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49318502/
1

This is a petition filed u/s.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.12 lakhs with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 2-8-2021 at about 9.20 a.m. when the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-JW-7705, Dombarahalli - Madanayakanahalli road, near Siddanahosahalli market, Dasanapura hobli, Bangalore, at that time, rider of the motor cycle bearing No.K A-03, EF-2077 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle from back side.

Due to impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and he was shifted to Madu hospital, T.Dasarahalli, Bangalore and took treatment as inpatient for 6 days,
operated Arthroscopic ACL reconstruction.
The petitioner spent Rs.2 lakhs for conveyance, food and nourishment charges.
The petitioner was doing tailor work in garments and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, petitioner is suffering from disability and discomforts.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.10 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte and respondent No.2 appeared through counsel before the Tribunal and filed written statement.
The respondent No.2 in the written statement contended that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner who was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-JW-7705.
Further contended that it is the self negligence and self suffering of the injuries of the petitioner.
Hence prays to dismiss the claim petition.

4. From the above said pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-03-EF- 2077 on 2-8-2021 at about 9.20 a.m. at Dombarahalli-Madanayakanahalli road, near Siddanahosahalli market, Daanapura hobli, Bangalore city?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined one witness as PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P13 documents.

The respondent No.2 got examined its Senior Manager-Legal as RW-1 and Swamy M.N vs Sathya Prakash on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49318502/
2 got marked Ex-R1.
6.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS  8. ISSUE NO.1:

In order to prove the rash and negligence, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 11 documents i.e., FIR,
complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, 133 notice, reply, wound certificate, charge sheet,
discharge summary, medical bills, aadhaar card.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent seriously disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle and contended that the petitioner himself by driving his motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner lost control over his vehicle and fell down from the bike and caused the accident by colluding with the police as implicated the offending vehicle in the accident.

Int he line of the defence, if the documents and materials and evidence are perused, soon after the accident, the Manoj brother of the petitioner lodge the complaint before Madanayakanahalli police station as per Ex-P2.
Based on which the FIR has been registered.

Thereafter the jurisdictional police have conducted a through and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet as per Ex-P8 against Thimmegowda who was riding the vehicle for the offence punishable u/s 279,338 of IPC and 187 of IMV Act by holding that on 3-8-2021 at about 9.20 a.m. in the Madanayakanahalli and Dombarahalli road, near Siddanahosahalli market, accused drove his Hero honda vehicle in high speed, rash and negligent manner and hit to the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-04-JW-7705 ridden by the petitioner from the back side and thereby caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained injuries.

10. Apart from this, on perusal of the spot mahazar, the spot of accident is a Dombarahalli-Madanayakanahalli main road and accident has been taken place in front of the Holibag and luggage shop at Siddanahosahalli market and road was running from north to south and width of the road is 21 feet tar road and accident has been taken place at the southern edge of the road within 5 feet distance from the southern edge.
Thus it clearly shows that both vehicles were moving in the same direction and the driver of the offending vehicle has hit to the back fo the motor cycle ridden by the petitioner.
From the very nature of the accident, it clearly shows that due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, accident has been taken place.

Moreover respondent has not examined the rider of the offending vehicle so as to state why and under what Swamy M.N vs Sathya Prakash on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49318502/
3 circumstances he hit to the back side of the petitioner's motor cycle.

sentences.text: The rider of the offending vehicle is a material witness, but none of the respondents has examined him and disprove the evidence of the PW-1 and the police documents.
The non examination of the rider of the offending vehicle is fatal to the case of the respondent.

Apart from this, on perusal of the vehicle seizure mahazar Ex-P4, it clearly shows that after finding out the offending vehicle, the owner was given the direction to produce the vehicle before the police station.

Accordingly the owner of the vehicle produced the vehicle before the police station, thereafter notice was issued to the RC owner respondent No.1 and the vehicle was seized and there was front side damages and back side number plate was also damaged and motor cycle examined.
Ex-P5 notice issued u/s 133 of IMV Act and ex-P6 reply given by the RC owner wherein respondent No.1 has given the reply stating that his vehicle was given to the accused Timmegowda for riding.
It is pertinent to note here that Ex-P6 is not at all denied by the either of the respondents.
From Ex-P4 to 6, it is clear that the offending vehicle has been involved in the accident.
Respondent No.1 has not stated any explanation and reasons as to why the damages was caused to his offending vehicle.
The very damages caused to the vehicle clearly shows that the offending vehicle has been involved in the accident.
11. Though learned counsel for the respondent cross examined PW-1 at length, but nothing was elicited from his mouth.
PW-1 has outrightly denied the suggestions made by the respondent counsel with regard to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner.
Even there are no materials to prove that the charge sheet is defective and collusive.
All these documents clearly shows that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.
Moreover all these documents have not at all been disputed by the respondents.

12. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
13. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

14. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

4
15. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the offending vehicle.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident she was aged 25 years.
The petitioner has produced aadhaar card as per Ex-P11, it reveals the year of birth of the petitioner was 4-1-1996.
So, as on the date of accident 2-8-2021
the petitioner was aged 25 years.
The petitioner has stated that he was doing Tailoring work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.

17. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:- As per the medical records i.e., Ex-P7- wound certificate reveals that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., (1) right knee joint swelling tenderum, deformity of right knee joint (2) right elbow and forearm- abrasion of 2 x 1 cm over elbow and upper forearm noted for which petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Madhu Ortho hospital from 2-8-2021 to 7-8-2021 for 6 days.

Further it reveals from the discharge summary that petitioner had undergone operation i.e., arthroscopic ACL reconstruction done on 3-8-2021.
18.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries she has become disabled and has lost her earning capacity.
Therefore he got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW-2 who has stated that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., right knee ACL tear.
The petitioner now complains of weakness and pain in the right knee, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg.
Petitioner has wasting of the right thigh muscles, restricted right knee movements.
X-ray fo the right knee shows evidence of ACL reconstruction with implant in situ.
PW-2 assessed the physical disability of right lower limb at 40% and to the wholebody at 13%.
PW-2 produced Ex-P12-clinical notes and Ex-P13-x-ray.
19 . During cross examination of PW-2 admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar - vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.

sentences.text: 20. Considering the nature of injuries, age of petitioner, occupation of petitioner, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner working as a tailor, certainly has to face some difficulty and disability to carry his avocation.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 10%, cannot be ruled out.

Swamy M.N vs Sathya Prakash on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49318502/
5
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 10%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 20 to 25 is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/-p.m.

Hence a sum of Rs.3,24,000/-
(Rs.15,000 X 12 X 18 X 10/100) is awarded under this head.
21. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., (1) right knee joint swelling tenderum, deformity of right knee joint (2) right elbow and forearm-abrasion of 2 x 1 cm over elbow and upper forearm noted for which petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Madhu Ortho hospital from 2-8- 2021 to 7-8-2021 for 6 days.
Further it reveals from the discharge summary that petitioner had undergone operation i.e., arthroscopic ACL reconstruction done on 3-8- 2021.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony due to the injuries sustained by him on account of the accidental injuries.
The petitioner being 25 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.75,000/- under this head.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the Madhu Ortho hospital, Bangalore for 6 days as inpatient and underwent operation i.e., arthroscopic ACL reconstruction on 3-8-2021.
It is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 8 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.60,000/- (15,000 X 4) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.

23. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Myadanahole,
Chitradurga and has taken treatment at Madhu hospital, Bangalore as inpatient for total 6 days and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of treatment, the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance,
extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.12,000/- under this head.

24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS :
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.

25. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Swamy M.N vs Sathya Prakash on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49318502/
6
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical bills Ex-P10 for Rs.87,492/-.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.87,492/- under the head of medical expenses.
26. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss
of future income

: 3,24,000=00 due to disability 2P Pain & sufferings :
75,000=00 3 Loss of income during : 60,000=00 laid-up period
4A Attendant charges, extra : 12,000=00 nutritious food &conveyance charges 5 Loss of future :R 25,000=00 amenities & 1, happiness
6 Medical expenses : 87,492=00 Total 5,83,492=00
Hence petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.5,83,492/-.
27. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
29. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
29. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,83,492/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
